lines.x: The spread between market foreign exchange rates and the central reference rate set by Bank Al-Maghrib exceeded 1% over consecutive sessions amid dollar demand.
Bank Al-Maghrib reported that the Moroccan dirham depreciated 1.7% against the US dollar and 0.6% against the euro between Nov 12 and Nov 17, with foreign reserves at MAD 512 billion.
Rhodium Group data shows Chinese firms completed $2.8 billion in Moroccan projects between Jan 2025 and June 2026, accounting for 60% of their 10-year total in the country.
S&P Global Ratings affirmed the BBB- long-term credit rating of Moroccan phosphate and fertilizer producer OCP S.A., citing capital discipline and strong liquidity management.
